mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand but a nascent housing recovery, which historically precedes a muted S&P 500 rally over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
regime_hint: late-cycle demand slowdown with housing stabilization
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in triggered episodes, or the pattern fails during a simultaneous labor market contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market that precedes a negative S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days due to elevated inflation and rate hike expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the pattern inverts during a deflationary shock.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals a supply-side expansion that boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0.3%) in at least 55% of triggered instances, or the pattern fails during a demand contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% and FEDFUNDS below 2% for the same month signals a disconnect between inflation and policy rates, which historically precedes a positive S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days as markets anticipate easing.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 50% of triggered months, or the pattern breaks during a wage-price spiral.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which consistently precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 6-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 65% of triggered episodes, or the pattern reverses during a supply-side boom.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate above 4% and a fall in average hourly earnings growth below 0.2% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the pattern fails during a strong productivity rebound.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between the housing starts index (HOUST) and S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days exists during periods of monetary easing, producing a reliable short-term bullish signal when HOUST rises month-over-month.
failure_condition: The correlation between month-over-month HOUST growth and subsequent 5-day S&P 500 returns falls below 0.3 or turns negative during any 12-month easing window.
